多様な提案を進化させ、意思決定を支える推薦手法「QD-Rec」を開発

ブログ：sakana.ai/qd-rec/
論文：arxiv.org/abs/2610.23470
GitHub：github.com/SakanaAI/QD-Rec

どの企業を買収候補として検討するか。どの顧客に新しい製品を提案するか。膨大な論文の中から、次に何を読むか。こうした意思 決定では、候補をスコア順に並べるだけでなく、「なぜ選ぶのか」「選んだ先にどのような可能性があるのか」を、異なる観点から比較できることが重要です。

一つの候補にも複数の有望な理由が考えられます。数千件、ときには1万件を超える候補それぞれについて、さまざまな仮説を生成・評価し尽くすには大きなコストがかかります。私たちは、限られた予算の中で「候補」と「仮説」の組を探索し、質が高く多様な提案を見つける問題を「オープンエンドな推薦」として捉えました。

QD-Recは、オープンエンドな探索の研究で発展してきた「Quality-Diversity（QD）」と呼ばれる進化的探索技術を、推薦に応用します。過去の評価結果をもとに次に調べる候補を選び、蓄積された仮説の着眼点をLLMが別の候補に応用したり、複数の仮説を組み合わせたりして、新しい提案を生成します。新しい切り口の提案は残し、似た提案同士ではより優れたものに更新することで、多様な仮説を次の発見の「踏み石」として活かし、推薦の集合を進化させていきます。

実験では、 企業の買収候補探索、架空の顧客プロファイルを使ったターゲティング、研究者向けの論文推薦などで検証しました。同じ評価回数のもとで比較したところ、多くの設定で、比較手法よりもQD-Recの方が評価が高く、より多様で多くの推薦を蓄積できました。

私たちが目指すのは、AIが人間の意思決定を代行することではなく、多様で有望な選択肢と、それらを比較・検討するための判断材料を提供することです。今回の成果を出発点に、QD-Recを次世代の意思決定を支える基盤技術へと発展させていきます。

The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scien…

The AI Scientist v3 is out: The Agentic Scientist.

GitHub: github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scien…
Blog: pub.sakana.ai/agentic-scient…
arXiv: arxiv.org/abs/2610.18933

The Agentic Scientist is the 3rd iteration of our automated AI Scientist research system, and the shift this time is from “one agent writes a paper” to “a scaffold of parallel agents orchestrates the full research loop.”

The system now orchestrates a pool of parallel workers that share memory and distilled conclusions. Crucially, it features Evidence Generation: isolated agents automatically run controlled baselines and ablations to prove why an idea actually works.

It works as a co-scientist. We used a development version as a co-scientist to explore biologically plausible learning rules. The agent handled the empirical heavy lifting, proposing mechanisms and running experiments. We stayed in the loop to steer direction, verify results, and moderate claims. That feels like the right division of labor for where the technology actually is.

This resulted in a new biologically plausible learning algorithm, and the resulting paper was accepted at ALIFE 2026 as an oral presentation.

We are also releasing AutoIllustrate. It generates editable draw.io vector figures instead of uneditable, hallucinated raster images. Real scientists need vectors, not pixels. I am an SVG junkie ;)

Incredible work by Robert Lange, Luca Grillotti, Yutaro Yamada, Rujikorn Charakorn, and the team!

Multi-Agent Self-Supervision: Recursive self-improvement through collective intelligence

Blog post: pub.sakana.ai/mass/ ⚖️

New paper from the team at Sakana AI:
Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS)

How do we keep improving AI when the tasks become too complex for humans to reliably evaluate?

For open-ended research, we eventually hit a "supervision bottleneck." If we use the model itself as the solver, optimizer, and evaluator, it gets trapped in a homogeneous loop, reinforcing its own blind spots rather than correcting them.

To break this loop, we drew inspiration from Marvin Minsky’s Society of Mind. What if you prompt a single model to organize copies of itself into a structured team, then distill what the team learned back into the base model?

MASS alternates between two loops:

1/ Workflow Optimization: the model iteratively evolves its own multi-agent workflows, figuring out how subagents should communicate and route information to each other.

2/ Workflow Internalization: fine-tune the shared model on the successful multi-agent trajectories so the coordination behavior gets baked into the weights.

After two cycles with a 27B open-weights model, performance improved 1.2-1.6x per output token on tough research benchmarks (MLR-Bench, ScienceAgentBench, DSBench).

Multi-agent traces were also much better training data than single-agent ones. The model learns faster from jointly learning high-level orchestration and bounded subagent execution. The results showing that the model can bootstrap its own coordination skills by organizing copies of itself into teams feels promising as a mechanism towards self-improvement.

Blog: pub.sakana.ai/mass/
Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176

Incredible work by Hyunin Lee, Jinglue Xu, Jeffrey Seely, Yujin Tang, and our collaborators from UC Berkeley (Somayeh Sojoudi, Matei Zaharia, Donghyun Lee)!
